parts.answer: Tension in the string to $A$ $=19.0\,\mathrm{N}$; tension in the string to $B$ $=20.4\,\mathrm{N}$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
*M1: Attempt to resolve horizontally or vertically to form an equation; correct number of terms; allow trigonometric-function mix-up and sign errors; do not award if the same tension is used for both strings (see special case).
A1: $T_A\cos35^\circ=T_B\cos40^\circ$; tensions must differ.
A1: $T_A\sin35^\circ+T_B\sin40^\circ=2.4g$. If the same tension is used, SC B2 only for this equation.
DM1: Attempt to solve for either tension from equations with the correct number of relevant terms; obtain at least one value.
A1: The published Answer cell prints "$T_1=20.4$ N and $T_2=19.0$ N". The published Guidance cell on the same line prints "$T_1=19.033621\ldots$, $T_2=20.353166\ldots$" and then, inconsistently, "awrt $20.4$ for $T_1$ www and $19(.0)$ for $T_2$". These statements are retained as printed. From the printed resolving equations, the string to $A$ (the $35^\circ$ string) has tension $19.033621\ldots$ N and the string to $B$ (the $40^\circ$ string) has tension $20.353166\ldots$ N.
Printed total: 5.
